ADOPTED VALUES: blueshift +197.5 km/s, EW 150.89 A, 263 usable C IV pixels spanning 1500.0-1599.9 A, scale 0.937. *** THE LUMINOSITIES ARE NOT USABLE AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED. The record reports log L1450 = 43.999 and log L1700 = 43.98 as 'measured', but measured straight from the chosen-run MXLO exposures over 1445-1465 A the observed f_lambda is 1.06e-14 erg/s/cm2/A, giving log lambdaL = 43.602 -- the pipeline value is 2.49 times high, 0.397 dex. For HST products flux x Continuum Normalisation IS the physical flux (verified against SDSS, median ratio 1.064), and for these IUE products that identity does not hold; the offset ran 2.3-5.5 across wavelength on an earlier check, so it may not even be a clean constant. THE BLUESHIFT AND EW ARE UNAFFECTED: the blueshift is a position and the EW is measured against the local continuum of the same spectrum, so a multiplicative scale divides out. WHICH SPECTRA WENT IN. The IUE chosen-run policy, the analogue of the HST single-visit policy: SWP 23799-24165, 5 exposures of the 41 the archive holds, run co-add S/N 18.7 at C IV. 3C 120's exposures span swp1357 to swp50192, roughly 1978 to 1994, and its C IV-region flux varies by a factor of three between runs, so co-adding all of them would average sixteen years of a variable Seyfert. It also does not work: the all-exposure co-add produced a spectrum with a NEGATIVE median where the data are +8.8e-15, C IV seven times too small, and ZERO usable C IV pixels in the fitter. From one run it is 263 usable pixels. GTR, asked whether one epoch at S/N 19 beats all epochs at S/N 37: "yes". WHY MODERATE AND NOT HIGH, WHICH IS GTR'S CALL AND IS SUPPORTED BY THE DATA. Si IV, an independent line, discriminates: over 1360-1440 A the residual is med -0.09 rms 0.16 on auto/moderate against med +0.13 rms 0.24 on high -- fifty per cent worse. LOW IS INADMISSIBLE: its sub-continuum veto carries 100.0 PER CENT of the clamped line flux, the signature that condemned several HST objects. So the admissible pair is moderate (+197.5) and high (+59.4), 138.1 km/s apart, EXACTLY TWO QUANTA, as GTR said. THE VETO IS COSMETIC: 23 pixels at 1500.0-1507.7 A, worst -10.2 per cent, carrying 0.000 of the clamped line flux. Scale 0.937, inside the healthy 0.88-1.00 band. The line is fully bracketed and C III] is covered (residual med +0.00 rms 0.17, n=128). INDEPENDENT CHECKS, AND THEY CLUSTER. The data's own half-flux point over the same window and continuum is +108.2 km/s; two hand measurements give +120.3 +- 141.5 (red anchor 1700-1705) and +123.7 +- 141.6 (1650-1690); and AMOGH'S INDEPENDENT FIT, from his own pipeline on the same archive, gives +21.9 with EW 133.2. The adopted +197.5 sits 1.3 quanta from the data half-flux and about 1.1 from both hand values. Amogh is 2.5 quanta below us and closer to the data half-flux than our fit is; that is recorded as the cross-check it is, not as a correction. The EWs agree well across all of them: 150.9 adopted, 136-138 by hand, 133.2 from Amogh. A RESERVATION RECORDED BUT NOT GRADED DOWN. Median per-pixel S/N in the C IV window is 1.32, inside the hollow-residual regime, so the low residual rms of 0.16 is partly the error bars being generous. The native chosen-run co-add is S/N 18.7; the dilution is the up-sampling onto the 69.03 km/s lattice, which oversamples IUE's 1.5 A pixels by about 4.7 and leaves neighbouring pixels correlated. The HST judging thresholds therefore do not transfer to IUE products, and the native numbers in iue/iue_assessment.csv are the honest ones.
